original_card.question: Does one changed supplier or assembly claim lack a source-bound independent check of a specific new implication?
methods: Independently reconstruct a coordinated frame/circuit change and its single-change control, then derive the complete rank and physical ledger.
Implement certified moment inequalities through a different exact enclosure method.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Demonstrate independence, source binding, positive cases and semantic failure controls. Name the existing checks and the missing coverage. More digits or another equivalent evaluation of an unchanged root is not by itself new verification coverage.

first_step.inspect: Read #2979 joint rank-7 end-frame proposal and the revision-6 evidence status. Its claimed kappa is not selected. Compare coordinated changes with the losing single-change controls and locate the complete physical ledger; an aggregate moment alone does not validate the mechanism.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Prioritize a bounded independent audit of #2979: reconstruct one joint group and its single-lowering control, check the declared frames/chronology, then trace changed children, idle widths and cleanup buffers into the complete invoice and both supplier caps. Choose one still-missing implication after checking existing audits. Stop with exact unresolved dependencies if full admission exceeds the session; do not launch a new lowering census on an unvalidated premise or substitute extra root digits for mechanism checking.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Independent pricing prevents unsupported frontier claims and can reveal genuine accounting slack.
allowed_variations: Reconstruct either a source ledger or a numeric enclosure with a different method.
scope_change_triggers: Importing the primary function and calling its output independent verification.
Promoting #2979 from merged source archive to validated supplier solely from author PASS receipts or aggregate pricing.

actual_scope: Prove a full retained directed sub-anchor box for every rational Gram factorization P=Q with nonempty canonical ties, and a modulo-four sufficient condition for good matched two-bit rows in general rational factorizations.
scope_change_reason: Handoff-first structural follow-up to PR3445's unresolved all-even asymmetric case and PR3454's finite Gram construction. Fresh overlap and scoped predecessor inspection found no general Gram statement. Baseline orientation passed; no selected frontier is changed.
bottleneck_link: Eliminates the entire admitted rational Gram subcase as a source of retained-box loss, while making higher-cancellation asymmetric obstructions explicit.
stop_rule: Check structural proof and canonical normalization within 20 minutes; finish a scoped proof and finite controls within 60 minutes, or release an exact handoff.
evidence: PROOF.md gives an arbitrary-size algebraic argument. verify.py checks finite modulo-four implications, rational canonical normalization, explicit retained witnesses and semantic controls. These finite checks supplement the proof and do not prove the unrestricted asymmetric problem.
author: Sagar Thakrar, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance including separate proof, executable-control and adversarial-review agents. Same-session reviews are not independent human acceptance or formal proof.

open_questions.question: Can the modulo-four partition cover asymmetric even-tie rows with unequal canonical anchors?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Such rows remain outside this sufficient condition and can obstruct a full box.
open_questions.first_step: Track the valuation-one contribution in the third coordinate instead of assuming it vanishes modulo four.
open_questions.blocked_by: Equal tied sets alone do not imply equal supports or matching colors.

open_questions.question: Does every twelve-line rational instance with nonempty ties have a box of size at least eight?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The general asymmetric target remains open after resolving the Gram subcase.
open_questions.first_step: Use the retained PR3445 obstruction reduction and separate higher-cancellation rows from the good rows classified here.
open_questions.blocked_by: The present theorem gives no adequate count of good rows in an arbitrary asymmetric factorization.
